challenge.method: Read the §1 definitions and tested three cases: an unrelated but licensable patent claim, a claim necessarily infringed only in combination with the submitted Work, and a claim implicated only by combining the Contribution with different software.
challenge.results: The unrelated claim fails the necessary-infringement condition. The submitted-Work combination satisfies that condition even if the Contribution alone does not, provided the Contributor can license the claim. A combination with different software alone does not satisfy either route. Section 1 ties Work to authorship made available under the license, Contribution to intentional authorized submission for inclusion, and Contributor to the Licensor or a party on whose behalf a received Contribution was incorporated.

limitations: Licensing authority and necessary infringement for a specific patent depend on external facts. The grant is subject to the license terms, including §3 termination.
reasoning: Section 3 imposes two cumulative limits on each Contributor's grant. The Contributor must be able to license the patent claim, and its Contributions must necessarily infringe that claim either alone or in combination with the Work to which they were submitted. The reopened 1,637-byte revision 1 claim had the requested SHA-256.
